title: Tulsi Gabbard Steps Down as Trump's Spy Chief
summary: A big change happened in Washington, D.C. Tulsi Gabbard, the director of national intelligence, resigned on Friday. That's the person in charge of all 18 U.S. spy agencies! She said she needs to focus on her family because her husband, Abraham, was diagnosed with a very rare bone cancer. Gabbard is a veteran and used to be a congresswoman from Hawaii. She was known for speaking out against wars. But this put her in a tough spot when President Trump decided to attack Iran earlier this year. Some reports say she didn't fully agree with the decision. During a meeting with lawmakers, she avoided saying whether she thought Iran was a big threat. She said it was the president's choice to strike, not hers. Gabbard's resignation means she is the fourth Cabinet member to leave during Trump's second term. Others who left include the heads of Homeland Security, Justice, and Labor. Now, the president will have to find someone new to lead the intelligence community.
why_it_matters: When leaders make big decisions about war, it can affect many people, and even top officials may have to choose between their job and their personal beliefs or family needs.

background_read: The United States has 18 spy agencies, including the CIA and the NSA, that gather secret information to keep the country safe. After the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001, the government created the job of Director of National Intelligence to help these agencies work together better.
Washington, D.C., is the capital city where the White House and Congress work. Iran is a country in the Middle East that has had long-standing tensions with the U.S.
Tulsi Gabbard, a former congresswoman from Hawaii and an Army veteran, took this role in President Donald Trump's second term. Her husband, Abraham, was diagnosed with a rare form of bone cancer.
Article_Structure: WHO: Tulsi Gabbard, the director of national intelligence.
WHAT: She resigned from her job, officially to focus on her family because her husband has cancer.
WHERE: Washington, D.C., the capital of the United States.
WHY: Her husband's illness was the main reason, but reports also suggest she didn't fully agree with the president's decision to attack Iran.

perspectives.description: Gabbard is putting her family first during a very difficult time, which many people see as a brave and caring choice.
Her sudden resignation could cause confusion among the spy agencies, especially when the U.S. is in a tense moment with Iran.
Cabinet changes are normal in any administration, and the president will now have to find a new person to lead the intelligence community, which happens regularly.
Whoever replaces Gabbard will have to quickly manage all 18 spy agencies and help the president make safe decisions about other countries.
